decisions.action: ADOPT through a pinned native R worker for selected observational FCI/RFCI profiles; no reimplementation first.
decisions.reason: Source exposes search cap, NAdelete, >= alpha, selected endpoint conversion, R dependency and license declarations.
decisions.admission: Retain CI status, threshold, conditioning trace, search limits, endpoint class and explicit unsupported graph refusals.
decisions.reject_or_defer: Do not call it universal FCI, port its branch path without trace evidence, or assume imports and rights are closed.

decisions.action: ADOPT only as a distinct mixed-data R profile behind the Rcpp wrapper.
decisions.reason: Pinned docs describe mixed input, orientation choices and row deletion under missingness; C++ implementation is R-hosted.
decisions.admission: Begin with explicit complete-case profile; record dropped rows and test family; separately assess MAR/MNAR target consequences.
decisions.reject_or_defer: Reject as a standalone C++ core or drop-in pcalg equivalent; no missing-data claim without new evidence.

decisions.action: ADOPT as a separate discovery-family comparator through its R package; do not port from wrapper evidence alone.
decisions.reason: Distinct information-theoretic, latent and stationary temporal modes, C++14 compilation, Rcpp/OpenMP build, GPL >=2 declaration.
decisions.admission: Match the named mode, data regime, output meaning, orientation confidence and temporal stationarity; retain source diagnostics.
decisions.reject_or_defer: Reject translation of a latent flag into a generic PAG or graph into an effect; direct native C++ packaging remains uninspected.

decisions.action: ADOPT in Python for a selected binary T-learner profile; wrapper preserves original fit objects and bootstrap.
decisions.reason: One shared control fit, sorted treatment labels, row-index resampling and separately controlled learner randomness are source-visible.
decisions.admission: Pass action labels, target rows, fit identities, row/cluster sampling unit, index RNG and learner RNG as distinct fields.
decisions.reject_or_defer: Defer multi-arm or clustered uncertainty claims until separately qualified; direct requirements are not a resolved lock.

decisions.action: ADOPT original JVM library for selected graph/search paths if its dependency and GPL obligations fit.
decisions.reason: Graph objects preserve endpoint types, but node lookup is identity-sensitive; selected core POM targets Java 21.
decisions.admission: Pin artifact, JDK, graph node map, endpoint vocabulary and the chosen search/options; run exact round-trip fixtures.
decisions.reject_or_defer: Do not treat newer nonstandard Python/R wrappers requiring JDK 25 as the same artifact or qualification.

decisions.action: ADOPT as an independent native C++ FCI/PAG comparator, not as a pcalg port.
decisions.reason: Possible-D-Sep, filtering, endpoint access and graph conversion have source-specific paths; dual LGPL-3-or-later/MIT statement has third-party caveats.
decisions.admission: Build only after dependency/rights inventory; compare graph-class outputs, node names, marks, missing-data behavior and diagnostics.
decisions.reject_or_defer: No runtime, binding, complete dependency-license or parity evidence; do not claim a cleared deployable product.

decisions.source: Proposed one-language rewrite of every selected package
decisions.action: REJECT as the current default architecture; retain narrow ports only after measured constraint.
decisions.reason: Method families, endpoint conventions, clocks, RNG coupling, missingness and license/dependency models differ.
decisions.admission: Require a failing native-worker need, bounded equivalence domain, exact fixtures, resource benchmark, ownership and maintenance case.
decisions.reject_or_defer: An attractive common API or matching graph name is not an evidence-based reason to reimplement.

limitations: Routes are proposals based on inspected pinned originals, not executable code or accepted integration.
No legal opinion, resolved transitive dependency lock, package installation or bank deployment review.
No finding of absence is made outside selected inspected source paths.
